data.description:
## Context / Problem

The project needs a repository-wide audit of documentation and source comments against the approved prose, punctuation, diction, audience, and content-placement standards. Future developers and agents need an evidence-based remediation proposal before any project file changes are authorized.

## Approach

Survey every maintained documentation surface and source comment category. Classify each finding by intended audience and durable record type. Compare factual claims with code, configuration, generated help sources, tests, ADRs, and ticket history. Record findings in a session log. Ask independent agents to inspect non-overlapping shards. Ask a later reviewer group to challenge the consolidated proposals for evidence, accuracy, completeness, placement, duplication, and writing conformance. Present the filtered proposal list for operator approval.

## Scope

- Root contributor and client documents, package metadata, repository policies, templates, and workflow text.
- Internal documents under `docs/`, including ADRs and indexes.
- External documents, packaged guides, command help, MCP descriptions, examples, and other shipped user guidance.
- Developer comments and docstrings in maintained source, scripts, tests, and configuration files.
- Relevant ticket history needed to distinguish historical records from current-state documentation.
- Read-only repository inspection. No project file edits, gates, commits, or pushes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The inventory covers maintained internal documents, external documents, packaged guides, generated and handwritten help, ADRs, relevant ticket records, comments, docstrings, examples, templates, scripts, configuration metadata, and contributor files. Verification uses session log entries that name each inspected shard and any explicit exclusion.
- [ ] Each retained proposal identifies repository evidence, the defect or gap, the intended audience and documentation type, the remediation action, and the destination. Verification uses the consolidated proposal list.
- [ ] Accuracy checks compare documentation claims with implementation, configuration, tests, and effective help output when those sources apply. Verification uses path and symbol citations in the proposal list.
- [ ] Independent agents inspect non-overlapping repository shards. A later reviewer group challenges the consolidated list for accuracy, completeness, placement, duplication, and prose compliance. Verification uses agent reports summarized in the session log.
- [ ] Project source files remain unchanged. Verification uses final worktree status and diff checks.
- [ ] The filtered remediation proposal is recorded on this ticket and presented to the operator for approval.
data.title: Audit documentation taxonomy, prose, and comment quality
